tier_rationale: Core function — opening and closing the door — runs entirely from the included wall control panel and 3-button RF remote with no network at all, and no account is needed to install the opener. The myQ account gates only the app, the camera, and notifications. Tier reflects the hardware; the vendor's conduct is scored separately at vendor_risk 3.
the_unplug_test: The door still opens. The wall button and the RF visor remote are hardwired and radio-paired to the opener, and neither has ever touched the internet. What you lose is everything Chamberlain added on top: the built-in camera goes dark, the myQ app cannot open the door from your phone, and you get no notifications that the door was left up. The battery backup still works. In short: you bought a garage door opener with a cloud camera bolted on, and unplugging the router leaves you with a garage door opener.
offline_losses: built-in security camera and any video
opening or closing the door from the myQ phone app

liberation.method: ratgdo — an ESPHome-based board wired to the opener's three terminals, speaking Chamberlain's Security+ protocol directly. Restores full local open/close/status plus light and motion, with no myQ account and no cloud. Home Assistant recommended it by name when Chamberlain cut off API access.

repairability.notes: Belt, sensors, wall control and remotes are all sold separately as spares. The logic board is the part that ages out.

sources.supports: Chamberlain blocked third-party API access to myQ, breaking integrations on devices already sold; the Home Assistant integration was removed in the 2023.12 release. Same post names ratgdo as a fully local ESPHome-based alternative compatible with Security+, installed by connecting three wires.
Retail listing confirming the B4643T ships with a wall control panel, a 3-button visor remote, a safety sensor kit and a wireless keypad — i.e. the door can be operated without any app.
Independent corroboration of the API shutdown and its timing relative to Chamberlain having previously dropped HomeKit and Google Assistant support.

notes: This record is why the ladder separates tier from vendor conduct. Chamberlain has done something genuinely hostile — revoking API access on hardware people already owned — but the door still opens when the internet is down, and calling it REJECT would send a reader looking for a problem they will not find. The honest reading is three separate facts: the hardware is D2, the vendor is a 3, and ratgdo makes the smart layer local again.
